items.title: Matcha in food: Healthy innovation or marketing gimmick?
items.summary: No longer confined to lattes, fancy drinks and desserts, matcha is increasingly being incorporated into a variety of savoury dishes, including nasi lemak, burgers and even fried catfish. He said that although matcha has antioxidant properties, various factors must be considered before labelling matcha-containing dishes as 'healthy' options. "Matcha's vibrant green colour makes it highly photogenic.

items.title: Guan Eng warns of SME liquidity crisis over RM30b delayed tax refunds
items.summary: Lim, who is the member of parliament for Bagan, pointed to the 2025 Federal Government Financial Statements, which show that outstanding tax refund liabilities decreased by RM3.425 billion, dropping from RM33.342 billion in 2024 to RM29.919 billion in 2025. To curb systemic delays, Lim proposed placing a strict RM10 billion cap on federal tax refund arrears. Outstanding tax refund commitments stood at RM21.836 billion in 2021, before climbing to RM25.721 billion in 2022 and RM25.511 billion in 2023.

items.title: Shuhaily: Public support gives me strength to face court proceedings
items.summary: SEPANG: Malaysia Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain has thanked the public for their prayers and messages of support ahead of his court proceedings today. Shuhaily said he would leave it to the court to conduct the legal proceedings in accordance with due process. "This is my last press conference regarding these legal proceedings.

items.title: Perak Perhilitan monitoring elephant herd after crop destruction complaints
items.summary: IPOH, Oct 21 — The Perak Department of Wildlife and National Parks (Perhilitan) has received six official complaints this year from oil palm smallholders in Kampung Perlop 1, Sungai Siput, over wild elephants destroying crops and plantation infrastructure. Its director, Dr Pazil Abdul Patah, said the herd is estimated at between three and eight elephants, believed to have come from the nearby Korbu Forest Reserve. "Perhilitan also believes these are the same elephants that encroached into fruit orchards around Bukit Bangkong, Chemor, on Oct 15, as both locations fall within the range of the Korbu Forest Reserve," he said in a statement.

items.title: Corporate-creative collaborations vital to boost Malaysian IPs, says Teo
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — Collaborations between corporate entities and local creative talent are vital in driving the growth of Malaysia’s creative sector and showcasing homegrown intellectual properties (IPs) to a broader audience. Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching said such strategic collaborations between corporate entities and homegrown creative teams allow local artists, animators, performers, and production personnel to showcase their skills on a wider stage. That connection helps our creative industry and our tourism industry grow together,” Teo said.

items.title: Malaysia calls for WHO-led pooled medicine purchasing amid supply risks
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — Malaysia has proposed that the World Health Organisation (WHO) Western Pacific Region (WPRO) urgently pilot a pooled procurement project for selected medicines to ensure drug security in the region. Health Minister Datuk Seri Dzulkefly Ahmad said the move was urgent as almost the entire region is facing critical challenges due to disrupted supply chains, market uncertainty, and high reliance on Active Pharmaceutical Ingredient (API) imports, with international geopolitical conflicts worsening the situation. He said the pooled procurement pilot project must involve selected medicines with healthy supplier competition and clear shared needs, and must be implemented transparently.

items.title: 'Anyone but Trump': Republicans face Latino backlash over immigration raids
items.summary: DORAL: For nearly two years, US President Donald Trump's heavy-handed deportation drive has sown fear in immigrant communities and generated a flood of grim headlines and social media videos. Now, with midterm elections looming, many Latino voters who helped propel Trump and his Republican Party to power in 2024 say they are fed up. In southern Florida's Doral, a mostly Latino community near Miami that is also home to one of Trump's golf clubs, residents told AFP that fears of potential raids have left businesses short-staffed and classrooms with fewer pupils.

items.title: Afdlin Shauki recounts five-hour ordeal trapped in Paris riots
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Actor and comedian Datuk Afdlin Shauki Aksan was trapped in Paris for five hours amid riots, with his wife and three-year-old daughter. In a Facebook post, Afdlin said he had travelled to France with his family to attend the International Market of Communications Programmes (Mipcom) in Cannes before spending time in Paris. "They immediately let us in and locked the door," he said.

items.title: Bukit Aman, Singapore police smash cross-border prostitution ring using Malaysia as base
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — Police have dismantled a cross-border prostitution syndicate that used Malaysia as an offshore operational command centre to market sex workers to clients in Singapore, arresting one local and 29 foreign nationals in a coordinated bilateral blitz. The joint crackdown, dubbed Op Noda – Rentas Sempadan, was mounted on Oct 20 by Bukit Aman’s Criminal Investigation Department (CID) alongside the Singapore Police Force (SPF) to stamp out networks managing online vice portals targeting Singaporean clientele. Checks on confiscated travel documents identified the foreign suspects as seven Chinese nationals and one Singaporean.

items.title: More than 1,500 public toilets upgraded under Housing Ministry initiative
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — The Housing and Local Government Ministry (KPKT) allocated RM154 million to local authorities (PBT) nationwide from 2023 to 2025 for the maintenance, repair and upgrading of public toilet facilities. Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming said the allocation had enabled 1,529 public toilets under the supervision of local authorities nationwide to be upgraded so far. He said KPKT would continue these efforts by allocating a special RM30 million annually from 2026 to 2030, bringing the total allocation to RM150 million for the repair and upgrading of public toilets managed by local authorities over the next five years.

items.title: Port Klang raid exposes alleged subsidised cooking oil diversion scheme
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Oct 21 — The Selangor Ministry of Domestic Trade and Cost of Living (KPDN) has successfully uncovered the misappropriation of subsidised controlled goods specifically one-kilogramme (kg) packets of cooking oil following a raid on a premises in the Port Klang area, with the seized items valued at RM133,950. Selangor KPDN director Muhamad Hanif Asa’ari said the suspected modus operandi involved bringing the packets of cooking oil to the premises, where they were mixed with used cooking oil in a dedicated storage tank. The raid uncovered a large quantity of boxes containing packeted cooking oil, as well as plastic packets that had already been cut open.

items.title: Health select committee taking haze concerns to Indonesian Embassy
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — The Parliamentary Special Select Committee on Health (JKPK) will submit a memorandum regarding the cross-border haze issue to the Indonesian Embassy today. Its chairman, Suhaizan Kaiat (PH-Pulai), said that the haze issue poses problems for the country across various aspects, such as the environment, public health, citizen safety, the national economy, and diplomatic relations between neighbouring countries. Meanwhile, Khoo Poay Tiong (PH-Kota Melaka) urged the government to take firm action against local companies allegedly involved in forest fires in Indonesia that caused the cross-border haze.

items.title: Perlis MB suspended from Bersatu for two terms
items.summary: PADANG BESAR: Perlis Menteri Besar Abu Bakar Hamzah has been suspended from Bersatu for two party election terms, effective Oct 13. Perlis Bersatu chairman Izizam Ibrahim confirmed the authenticity of a suspension letter dated Oct 14 and signed by Bersatu Disciplinary Board chairman Datuk Mohd Radzi Manan. According to the letter, the party's Disciplinary Board, which met on Oct 13, decided to suspend Abu Bakar's membership rights for two party election terms under Clause 22.5.

items.title: New haj plan could cut waiting time to under 70 years, says minister
items.summary: He said this would depend, among other factors, on the number of depositors who meet the stipulated minimum savings requirement, Malaysia’s official haj quota in the future, and current developments, particularly in the Holy Land. “Beginning Jan 1, 2029, the haj waiting list will be systematically and automatically reorganised based on registration dates among those who have reached the minimum savings threshold of RM15,000. Zulkifli said registered haj depositors would be given a transition period of more than two years, until Dec 31, 2028, to meet the minimum savings target of RM15,000.

items.title: Shuhaily charged with hurting two Special Branch policemen
items.summary: SEPANG: Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain pleaded not guilty at the magistrate's court to two counts of voluntarily causing hurt to two Special Branch policemen last month. Shuhaily, 54, was charged with voluntarily causing hurt to Lance Corporals Muhammad Ekmal Sofwan Driman and Mohammad Faiz Muhamad Saman, 40, on Sept 28 at Kuala Lumpur International Airport Terminal 1. Shuhaily, who stood near the dock, told magistrate Khairatul Animah Jelani that he understood the charges and claimed trial.

items.title: New MyKad security features, transboundary haze measures among topics in Dewan Rakyat
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — The justification for introducing a new-generation MyKad, its security levels, and cooperation between Malaysia and Indonesia in tackling cross-border haze are among topics expected to take center stage during the Dewan Rakyat sitting today. Datuk Iskandar Dzulkarnain Abdul Khalid (Kuala Kangsar) wants the Minister of Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability to explain the diplomatic actions and cooperation implemented by the Malaysian government with the Indonesian government to mitigate the risk of cross-border haze. The sitting will then resume the debate on the Supply Bill 2027 at the policy stage following the tabling of Budget 2027 by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, who is also the Minister of Finance, on October 9.

items.title: Iskandar Malaysia hits RM525bil, sets sights on bigger gains
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Iskandar Malaysia has attracted RM525.26 billion in investments over two decades, exceeding its original RM383 billion target by RM142.26 billion, as Johor's flagship economic corridor shifts towards higher-value industries and deeper cross-border integration to sustain its next phase of growth. The next phase will prioritise advanced manufacturing, digital and data-driven industries, modern logistics, and high-value financial and business services, positioning Iskandar Malaysia to capture a greater share of regional and global economic activity. "For the next development phase, emphasis will be placed on increasing productivity and high-value economic activity, including advanced manufacturing, digital and data-driven industries, and logistics, as well as financial and business services," IRDA said in a statement.

items.title: Haze in Malaysia: 22 areas still at ‘Unhealthy’ air quality levels
items.summary: No station recorded very unhealthy or hazardous levels. Bukit Rambai in Melaka recorded the highest reading at 174, up from 166 yesterday afternoon. Johor had seven unhealthy stations.

items.title: Minimum 30 per cent Bumiputera equity requirement retained - Economy Ministry
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The minimum 30 per cent Bumiputera equity requirement remains in place in line with the Property Acquisition Guidelines (GPPH), which took effect on July 13, 2022, and is subject to approval by the Economy Ministry. The ministry said the government is committed to ensuring that the country's strategic assets, particularly those owned by government-linked companies (GLCs) and government-linked investment companies (GLICs), contribute more effectively to the Bumiputera economic empowerment agenda. The ministry said that after taking into account stakeholders' views and reviewing the proposed implementation of the requirement, the government has decided to enforce it through administrative measures to ensure that all GLCs and GLICs implement the Bumiputera economic empowerment agenda.

items.title: Retiree sells house, loses RM132,590 in forex scam
items.summary: TELUK INTAN: A 73-year-old retiree lost RM132,590 in a bogus foreign exchange (forex) investment scheme, with part of the money coming from the sale of his house. Hilir Perak district police chief assistant commissioner Chua Kok Lian said the victim lodged a police report on Monday after realising that he had likely fallen victim to the scam. However, Chua said the victim became suspicious when he could no longer access the investment system on Sept 14.

items.title: Early savings pave the way for a child's future
items.summary: A CHILD'S future is full of possibilities. Many children start developing their ambitions and dreams young. For parents, preparing for their children's future is not something that can be achieved overnight.

items.title: Penang ramps up efforts to tackle Parit Cina, Sungai Kereh pollution
items.summary: State Local Government and Town & Country Planning Committee chairman Jason H’ng Mooi Lye said the initiative was among the state government’s efforts to address the pollution of Sungai Kereh, an issue that has persisted for decades. H’ng said the state government is also strengthening pig farm waste management through a short-term action plan involving the transportation of waste to biogas plants, and a long-term plan involving a proposal to construct a biogas plant facility in Kampung Selamat, as presented by the Penang Veterinary Services Department on May 11. Under the short-term plan, he said solid and liquid waste from pig farms in Kampung Selamat is being transported to the biogas plant in Ampang Jajar.

items.title: 22 areas record unhealthy air quality, Bukit Rambai highest at 174 API
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Twenty-two areas nationwide recorded unhealthy air quality as of 8am today. In Kuala Lumpur, Batu Muda and Cheras each recorded an API reading of 159, while Putrajaya recorded 158. Meanwhile, APIMS data showed that 39 other air quality monitoring stations nationwide recorded moderate API readings, while seven areas recorded good air quality.

items.title: PKR rejects Mukhriz claim linking party to PN deregistration
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) has denied any involvement in the Registrar of Societies’ (RoS) decision to cancel the registration of Perikatan Nasional (PN) today. PKR secretary-general Datuk Fuziah Salleh described as defamatory the allegation by Parti Pejuang Tanahair (Pejuang) president Datuk Seri Mukhriz Mahathir that the decision was made on PKR’s recommendation. “I consider the use of slides that were never presented, in an attempt to link PKR to the RoS decision on PN, to be defamatory.

items.title: Takiyuddin challenges Bersatu Youth to prove allegations over PN deregistration
items.summary: KOTA BARU: Perikatan Nasional secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan has challenged Bersatu Youth to substantiate its allegations against him and PN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar over the coalition's deregistration. "We challenge him (Bersatu Youth information chief Harris Idaham Rashid) to prove his allegations. Yesterday, Bersatu Youth blamed Takiyuddin and Samsuri for the coalition's deregistration by the Registrar of Societies Malaysia (RoS).

items.title: Border agency chief Shuhaily in court over alleged KLIA assault of two Special Branch cops
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — Malaysia Checkpoints and Border Agency (MCBA) director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain arrived at the Sepang Magistrate’s Court this morning to face two charges of assault linked to an altercation with two Special Branch officers at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA). Security was tight across the court grounds, with an augmented contingent of police and Rela personnel restricting compound vehicle access strictly to authorised court staff and law enforcement officers, NST reported. Lending a show of solidarity at the court complex was Port Klang MCBA commander Datuk Nik Ezanee Mohd Faisal.

items.title: Oil rises on Middle East supply worries
items.summary: Brent crude futures rose 85 cents, or 0.78 per cent, to US$109.64 per barrel as of 0022 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude rose 76 cents, or 0.78 per cent, to US$98.58 per barrel. The November contract for US West Texas Intermediate crude, which expired on Tuesday, settled down US$1.87, or 1.8 per cent, at US$101.79.

items.title: Government open to KWAP, EPF RCI subject to findings, says Azalina
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 —The government is open to considering a proposal to establish a Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) into the Retirement Fund (Incorporated) (KWAP) and the Employees Provident Fund (EPF), should the need arise. Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said this would apply if there is concrete information, evidence, or findings indicating a necessity for a comprehensive and independent public inquiry. “If the findings indicate a clear public need and interest for a special inquiry, a proposal to establish a Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) may be duly considered.

items.title: 6,346 MyKiosk units operational nationwide
items.summary: Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming said the remaining 897 units, or 12 per cent, were vacant, based on data and operational reports submitted by state governments and local authorities. "The MyKiosk programme, implemented through the Local Government Department, aims to improve the socioeconomic status of local traders by providing standardised, safe and conducive business premises at affordable rental rates," he said in a written parliamentary reply published on Parliament's website yesterday. Nga said the ministry was working closely with local authorities to increase occupancy rates and ensure the kiosks were fully utilised, with four strategic measures being implemented to address vacancies.

items.title: Govt open to RCI into KWAP, EPF if evidence warrants probe
items.summary: Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said issues involving the management of public funds, including governance and investment decisions, would continue to be examined based on facts and evidence through appropriate oversight mechanisms. "Should further scrutiny establish a clear need and public interest in a special investigation, the proposal to establish an RCI may be considered accordingly," she said in a written parliamentary reply. Shahidan also sought clarification on the criteria used by the government to determine whether an RCI was necessary for institutions managing public funds.

items.title: Malaysia eyes bigger role in global seabed mapping
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia is strengthening its role in global seabed mapping by hosting an international meeting and data sprint. The event brings together experts from 33 countries to advance ocean mapping and data sharing. Royal Malaysian Navy chief Admiral Tan Sri Dr Zulhelmy Ithnain officiated at the opening of the Seabed 2030 Indo-Pacific Ocean Mapping Meeting and Data Sprint 2026 here.

items.title: Haj waiting period could fall from 150 years to below 70
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The haj waiting period could be more than halved, from about 150 years to less than 70, under the Haj Preparation Plan – Seruan Istito'ah. "Depositors who had already registered for haj would be given a transition period of more than two years, until Dec 31, 2028, to meet the minimum savings requirement of RM15,000. Zulkifli said depositors who had registered but had yet to meet the RM15,000 requirement would be included in the active haj waiting list once they fulfilled the savings requirement.

items.title: Ringgit opens higher on strong domestic economic data
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit opened higher against the US dollar on Wednesday, supported by strong domestic economic data that strengthened expectations of a possible normalisation of the overnight policy rate (OPR). At 8am, the ringgit strengthened to 4.0795/0850 against the greenback from Tuesday's close of 4.0805/0845. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said robust economic indicators, particularly export growth and gross domestic product (GDP) expansion, provide support for the local currency.

items.title: New MyKad's security, efforts to tackle cross-border haze among topics in Dewan Rakyat
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The justification for introducing a new-generation MyKad, its security levels, and cooperation between Malaysia and Indonesia in tackling cross-border haze are among topics expected to take center stage during the Dewan Rakyat sitting today. Datuk Iskandar Dzulkarnain Abdul Khalid (Kuala Kangsar) wants the Minister of Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability to explain the diplomatic actions and cooperation implemented by the Malaysian government with the Indonesian government to mitigate the risk of cross-border haze. The sitting will then resume the debate on the Supply Bill 2027 at the policy stage following the tabling of 2027 Budget by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, who is also the finance minister, on Oct 9.

items.title: US coaxing refiners to produce more diesel as prices surge, energy officials say
items.summary: TITUSVILLE/HOUSTON: Two top US Energy Department officials said on Tuesday they were working with refiners at home and abroad to boost fuel output as a diesel shortage has raised prices, driving dissatisfaction among voters with the White House ahead of the November midterm elections. Retail diesel prices averaged about US$6.32 a gallon on Tuesday, according to motorist group AAA. The Trump administration has taken several steps to try to lower fuel prices that have surged since the start of the Iran war on Feb 28, including relaxing restrictions on Russian diesel exports, invoking the Defense Production Act to boost output and allowing commercial vehicles to run on red-dyed diesel normally limited to off-road equipment.

items.title: MCBA chief arrives at court over alleged assault on two policemen [WATCH]
items.summary: SEPANG: Malaysia Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain arrived at the court complex to face two charges over an alleged assault involving two Special Branch policemen. Security was tight at the court complex, with a heavy presence of police personnel and Rela members. Only court staff and police personnel were allowed to park within the compound.

items.title: Malaysians to gain from wider access to affordable essentials
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysians will benefit from wider access to affordable essentials, improved distribution in rural areas and stronger consumer protection under the 2027 Budget, as the government steps up efforts to address the rising cost of living. The RM80 billion allocation for aid, subsidies and incentives aims to ease financial pressures on households while supporting businesses, rural entrepreneurs and the creative industry. The measures, backed by additional funding for affordable sales programmes and enforcement, intends to make essential goods more accessible, improve market fairness and create new economic opportunities.

items.title: Malaysia posts RM1.57tril exports in nine months, but growth may cool
items.summary: Exports rose 34 per cent year-on-year, supported by strong electrical and electronics (E&E) shipments and expanding demand in non-traditional markets. Malaysia External Trade Development Corp (Matrade) today said total trade grew 30.1 per cent to RM2.91 trillion during the period, while imports increased 25.7 per cent to RM1.34 trillion. Downstream palm oil-based manufactured products, particularly oleochemicals, also recorded double-digit export growth.

items.title: Malaysia mulls CPO tax waiver as palm oil stocks hit record 3.5mil tonnes
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia is considering waiving the crude palm oil (CPO) export tax to help clear record-high stockpiles and narrow the pricing gap with Indonesia. The proposal comes as Malaysia's palm oil inventories climbed to 3.5 million tonnes last month, putting growing pressure on exporters because Indonesian palm oil continues to enjoy a significant price advantage. ESG Malaysia executive director Dr Harald Sippel said a temporary waiver of crude palm oil (CPO) export tax could help Malaysia reduce swelling inventories and boost exports.

items.title: Man allegedly behind 'targeted' attack on Australian lawmaker due in court
items.summary: WANGARATTA: The man alleged to have critically wounded Australian lawmaker Helen Haines in a "targeted" attack was due to appear in court on Wednesday, as police warned that growing extremism online was fuelling political polarisation. However, police said on Wednesday they were examining all possible leads, including whether he may have held radical anti-government views. Australian Federal Police (AFP) Commissioner Krissy Barrett said there was a growing level of "extremist views" online.

items.title: Musk: SpaceX and Tesla's Terafab targets 2028 for volume chip production
items.summary: SAN FRANCISCO: The chip manufacturing joint venture between SpaceX and Tesla called Terafab aims to reach volume production by the third quarter of 2028, Elon Musk said on a SpaceX conference call on Tuesday. On Tuesday, Musk said that internally, Terafab aims to have a first test chip, using static random-access memory (SRAM) circuits, functional in roughly May or June of next year at the Terafab research facility in Austin. Musk cautions on ambitious dates Musk has a history of setting timelines that his companies have missed.

items.title: BBC slashes 100 jobs, closes two channels
items.summary: LONDON: The BBC announced more than 100 job cuts and the closure of two channels on Tuesday as the cash-strapped UK broadcaster seeks to save £500 million (US$668 million) over the next two years. The job cuts represent £5.5 million in savings, Jupp said in the note sent to AFP. The BBC also said it would end broadcasts on BBC Scotland and BBC Three, a youth-oriented channel, with both remaining available on its online iPlayer streaming platform.

items.title: Netflix shares drop on slowing engagement, revenue growth
items.summary: SAN FRANCISCO: Netflix shares fell more than five per cent on Tuesday afternoon after its quarterly earnings report failed to ease investor concerns about slowing viewer engagement and revenue growth. In its third quarter, which ended in September, Netflix recorded US$12.87 billion in revenue and US$3.7 billion in net income, above investor expectations, according to FactSet. In July, Netflix said subscribers had spent 97 billion hours watching content in the first half of the year, a two per cent increase from the first half of 2025.

items.title: Trump says he wants Zelenskyy to 'make a deal' with Russia
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump on Tuesday urged Volodymyr Zelenskyy to make a deal with Russia, increasing pressure on the Ukrainian leader even as Moscow continues its war, launched four years ago. "We want Zelenskyy to make a deal. He can make a deal.

items.title: Experts: It could be gloves off between Pas and Bersatu in Melaka [WATCH]
items.summary: International Islamic University Malaysia political scientist Associate Professor Dr Syaza Shukri said the two parties had previously held back from conflict. "Pas has been clear about not working with Bersatu. So now, Bersatu can retaliate," she said.

items.title: Why won’t the rain wash away Malaysia’s haze? Experts explain what’s keeping the smoke coming
items.summary: According to Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) director-general Mohd Hisham Mohd Anip, rainfall can provide only temporary relief as long as smoke continues to arrive from Indonesia. “The haze currently affecting the country is caused by transboundary haze, whereby smoke from fire-affected areas in neighbouring countries is carried into Malaysian airspace. “Rainfall during the monsoon transition can only temporarily reduce haze conditions.

items.title: Haze is making pets sick too: Malaysian vets report cats suffering asthma attacks, dogs needing oxygen therapy
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Oct 21 — Haze and poor air quality are taking a toll on pets, with veterinarians reporting respiratory problems in cats, birds and dogs, including cases requiring oxygen therapy, as polluted air continues to affect parts of Malaysia. Dr Wendy Cheng of Noah’s Ark Veterinary Clinic said fine particles in polluted air, including PM2.5, could irritate animals’ respiratory systems and aggravate existing heart or lung conditions. — Picture courtesy of Dr Wendy Cheng Meanwhile, Sabah-based veterinarian Dr Randolf Paza, who has 37,000 followers on Facebook and runs the Dr Haiwan Sabah Instagram account, said veterinary clinics and animal shelters in Peninsular Malaysia had also encountered animals experiencing respiratory problems amid unhealthy air quality.

items.title: Haze: Schools remain open in six states, KL and Putrajaya tomorrow, outdoor activities halted
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — Schools in Melaka, Selangor, Negeri Sembilan, Perak, Pahang and Penang, as well as Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya, will operate as usual tomorrow, with outdoor activities have been suspended due to the haze. In NEGERI SEMBILAN, the state Education Department (JPNS) said in a statement today that all educational institutions under the Ministry of Education (MOE) would operate as usual. In PAHANG, the state Education Department said schools in Rompin, Bentong and Cameron Highlands would operate tomorrow, but all outdoor activities would be suspended.

items.title: From Waze to TuJu? Anwar backs Malaysian navigation app over data security concerns
items.summary: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said this alternative has been proposed due to security risks concerning information and data on citizens’ movements, given that the Waze application is subject to the laws of the Israeli government. He noted that this matter was among the topics discussed while chairing the third meeting of the National Cyber Security Committee (JKSN) today, which aimed to examine evolving cyber threats and strengthen the nation’s preparedness and digital sovereignty. “Also discussed were the implementation of the Cyber Security Act 2024, the security of MyDigital ID, preparations to counter threats from quantum computing through post-quantum cryptography (PQC), emerging threats involving autonomous artificial intelligence, and the protection of National Critical Information Infrastructure (NCII).

items.title: No action against UM student over viral ‘tough’ question, says Zambry
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 20 — The Higher Education Ministry (MOHE) and Universiti Malaya (UM) have no intention of taking action against the student who went viral recently after asking a “tough” question during the i-Future programme. Minister Datuk Seri Zambry Abd Kadir said the ministry maintained its position that students’ right to freedom of expression must be respected, while condemning any form of abuse, insults or threats directed at the student on social media. Respect students’ right to speak up.

items.title: No driving licences without tests: JPJ warns against fake TikTok promotions
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 20 — The Road Transport Department (JPJ) has denied the authenticity of a TikTok advertisement offering driving licences without the need to take a test. In a statement today, JPJ said it received complaints regarding the advertisement, which used an account under the name ‘Ahmad Mushidi’. “JPJ wishes to emphasise that the advertisement and the account belonging to the individual named Ahmad Mushidi are fake,” the statement read.

items.title: Kampar woman loses over RM129,000 in online job scam
items.summary: Kampar District Police Chief Supt Mohamad Nazri Daud said that his department received a report yesterday from the 34-year-old victim. “Initial police investigations found that the victim saw an offer for a part-time job related to hotel bookings through social media. “The victim received a message from an unknown individual offering the job.

items.title: Terengganu, Kelantan, Kedah and Perlis record highest drug abuse rates
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 20 — Terengganu, Kelantan, Kedah and Perlis recorded the highest rates of drug or substance addiction and abuse in the country, based on statistics up to June 2026, said National Anti-Drugs Agency (Nada) director-general Datuk Ruslin Jusoh. He said Terengganu recorded the highest rate at 735 individuals per 100,000 population, followed by Kelantan (694), Kedah (669) and Perlis (646). Ruslin said a total of 130,307 drug and substance abuse cases were recorded nationwide during the same period, equivalent to a rate of 381 individuals per 100,000 population.

items.title: Selangor Education Department cooperating with probe into schoolgirl’s death
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Oct 20 — The Selangor State Education Department (JPN Selangor) will fully cooperate with the authorities’ investigations into the death of a Year One pupil after she experienced breathing difficulties at a school in Sepang. In a statement today, JPN Selangor said the girl was reported to have had breathing difficulties at school and was taken to hospital for treatment. “JPN Selangor extends its condolences and deepest sympathies to the pupil’s family.

items.title: Police record statements over podcast video on alleged drug trafficking
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — Police have opened an investigation into the circulation of a podcast video alleging that drug trafficking activities were taking place at a house of worship near the Sentul District Police Headquarters (IPD) here. Sentul district police chief ACP Anuar Bakri Abdul Salam said the investigation was being conducted under Section 505(b) of the Penal Code and Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998. He said the investigation was initiated following a police report lodged by the chairman of the Marathadi Madurai Veeran Temple in Kuala Lumpur last Sunday to strongly deny the allegations made in the video.

items.title: Saifuddin Nasution urges Asean to translate anti-crime pledges into results
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 20 — Asean must ensure that all commitments and cooperation frameworks agreed upon to combat transnational crime are translated into concrete action specifically in addressing online fraud, money laundering, and human smuggling. Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the success of regional security cooperation should not be measured by the number of agreements reached, but rather by the effectiveness of enforcement actions taken against criminal networks. Saifuddin Nasution highlighted that as Malaysia prepares to chair Asean in 2025, the country has laid a crucial foundation for regional security cooperation through the adoption of the Asean Plan of Action to Combat Transnational Crime (2026-2035) and the Melaka Declaration.

items.title: Fahmi calls for stronger Asean cooperation on child online safety
items.summary: BALI, Oct 20 — Asean countries must work together to protect children from growing online threats despite differences in their laws and approaches to internet safety, said Malaysia’s Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil. He said countries in the region shared the challenge of keeping the internet safe for children and needed to strengthen cooperation to address these threats. Fahmi said Malaysia wanted to ensure that children below the age of 16 were unable to open social media accounts, although approaches to online safety for children could differ between Malaysia, Indonesia, Singapore and other Asean countries.

items.title: Anwar backs efforts to strengthen IsDB Centre of Excellence in Kuala Lumpur
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has welcomed efforts to strengthen the Islamic Development Bank (IsDB) Centre of Excellence in Kuala Lumpur, positioning it as a hub for the sharing of knowledge and expertise. He noted that Malaysia is recognised for its experience in empowering micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs), strengthening economic resilience, and generating employment opportunities, expertise and experience that could potentially benefit other IsDB member countries. The IsDB Centre of Excellence in Kuala Lumpur, launched in 2019, serves as a strategic platform for the transfer of technology, expertise, and best practices in Islamic finance from Malaysia to the 56 other IsDB member countries.

items.title: Selangor Sultan cautions royal family members against exploiting royal status
items.summary: KLANG, Oct 20 — Sultan of Selangor Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah has warned members of the Selangor royal family against exploiting their royal status to deceive others for personal gain. “We have a responsibility to protect the reputation of the Selangor royal family and institution. The Sultan also urged family members to maintain strong bonds, avoid hostility and prevent minor disagreements from causing divisions within the extended royal family.

items.title: Muhyiddin saddened by Perikatan deregistration, warns against abuse of power in coalitions
items.summary: In a statement, Muhyiddin, who founded PN, said he was saddened by the coalition's deregistration. "However, this decision is a reminder to any party leading a coalition to act fairly towards all member parties and to always comply with the party constitution and the Societies Act 1966," he said. Muhyiddin also cautioned against the misuse of power and position within a political coalition for the benefit of a particular party or group.
